title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: UtilsFaustSV provides utility functions extract work outputs FAUST (Functional Annotation Unsupervised T-cell clustering) use downstream analyses. main use cases package : Extracting FCS files cells belonging FAUST-identified populations analysis tools Getting cell counts populations defined using subset markers FAUST used clustering Visualizing population frequencies across samples key feature package ability define populations using subset markers FAUST used. allows : Extract broader cell lineages (e.g., CD3+CD4+ cells regardless markers) Combine multiple FAUST clusters single population Get counts FCS files cell types defined different levels granularity

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
code: library(UtilsFaustSV)  # Set the path to your FAUST project directory project_path <- "/path/to/faust/project"

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: running FAUST, output stored directory structure like:
code: project_path/ └── faustData/     ├── faustCountMatrix.rds         # Count matrix     ├── exhaustiveFaustCountMatrix.rds     ├── metaData/     │   ├── analysisMap.rds     │   ├── scampClusterNames.rds     │   └── activeChannels.rds     ├── sampleData/     │   └── <sample_name>/     │       └── faustAnnotation.csv  # Per-cell annotations     └── fcsData/                     # Output FCS files (created by this package)

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: First, ’s useful understand markers FAUST used many expression levels identified : returns named numeric vector : - Names marker names - Values number expression levels (typically 2 binary +/-)
code: # Get markers and their levels markers <- faust_marker_get_usage(project_path = project_path) print(markers)

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: Populations can defined several ways:

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: common way define population using named character vector names markers values expression levels:
code: # CD3+CD4+ cells pop_cd4 <- c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+")  # CD3+CD8+ cells pop_cd8 <- c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "-", "CD8-IgD" = "+")

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: markers 2 levels, can use descriptive levels: -: Negative +: Positive (2-level markers) Dim: Dim expression (3-level markers) Bright: Bright expression (3-level markers) MedLow, MedHigh, VeryBright: 4-level markers

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: can also use numeric levels (1 = lowest, 2 = next, etc.):
code: # Equivalent to c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+") pop_cd4_numeric <- c("CD3" = 2, "CD4" = 2)

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: Use list define multiple populations:
code: # Both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells pop_both <- list(   c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+", "CD8-IgD" = "-"),   c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "-", "CD8-IgD" = "+") )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: faust_fcs_write() function exports cells matching population definition FCS files:
code: # You need the original GatingSet that FAUST used # gs <- flowWorkspace::load_gs("/path/to/gatingset")  # Export CD3+CD4+ cells faust_fcs_write(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),   fr_source = gs )  # Files are saved to: # project_path/faustData/fcsData/<pop_definition>/

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
code: faust_fcs_write(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),   fr_source = gs,   dir_save = "/path/to/output" )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
code: # By sample name faust_fcs_write(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),   fr_source = gs,   sample = c("sample1.fcs", "sample2.fcs") )  # By index faust_fcs_write(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),   fr_source = gs,   sample = 1:5 )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: data transformed FAUST analysis, can back-transform exporting:
code: # Back-transform data that was asinh-transformed # (sinh is the inverse of asinh) faust_fcs_write(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),   fr_source = gs,   trans_fn = sinh )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: Get full FAUST count matrix:
code: counts <- faust_count_get(project_path = project_path)

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: Get counts populations matching definition: returned data frame includes: - Sample identifiers - Total counts classified counts - Counts matching population subset
code: # Get counts for all CD3+CD4+ subsets cd4_counts <- faust_count_get_pop(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+") )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: using list populations, counts summed:
code: # Get summed counts for T cell subsets t_cell_counts <- faust_count_get_pop(   project_path = project_path,   pop = list(     "CD4+ T cells" = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+", "CD8-IgD" = "-"),     "CD8+ T cells" = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "-", "CD8-IgD" = "+")   ) )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: default, FAUST filters rare populations. include populations:
code: all_counts <- faust_count_get_pop(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),   exhaustive = TRUE )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: faust_count_plot() function creates box plots population frequencies: Plots saved : project_path/faustData/plotData/pop_stats/<population_name>.png
code: # Plot all CD4+ T cell subsets faust_count_plot(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+", "CD8-IgD" = "-") )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
code: faust_count_plot(   project_path = project_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),   font_size = 12,   point_size_max = 3,   p_width = 50,   p_height = 20 )

title: Getting Started with UtilsFaustSV
text: ’s complete workflow extracting analyzing T cell subset:
code: library(UtilsFaustSV)  # Set paths project_path <- "/path/to/faust/project"  # 1. Check available markers markers <- faust_marker_get_usage(project_path = project_path) print(markers)  # 2. Define populations of interest cd4_memory <- c(   "CD3" = "+",   "CD4" = "+",   "CD8-IgD" = "-",   "CD45RA" = "-",   "CCR7" = "+" )  # 3. Get counts counts <- faust_count_get_pop(   project_path = project_path,   pop = cd4_memory )  # 4. Create visualization faust_count_plot(   project_path = project_path,   pop = cd4_memory )  # 5. Export FCS files for further analysis faust_fcs_write(   project_path = project_path,   pop = cd4_memory,   fr_source = gs  # Your GatingSet )

what: Write FAUST Populations to FCS Files
title: Additional functions to extract and plot FAUST output
text: Export cells matching population definition FCS files. Populations can defined using subset markers, enabling extraction broader cell types:
code: # Export CD3+CD4+ cells (defined by any number of levels of other markers) faust_fcs_write(   project_path = proj_path,   pop = c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),   fr_source = gs  # GatingSet used by FAUST )  # Export multiple populations at once faust_fcs_write(   project_path = proj_path,   pop = list(     c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+"),     c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "-", "CD8-IgD" = "+")   ),   fr_source = gs )

title: Additional functions to extract and plot FAUST output
text: Extract counts cells matching specific population definitions:
code: # Get counts for all subsets matching an annotation faust_count_get_pop(   project_path = proj_path,   pop = c("CD4" = "-", "CD8-IgD" = "+") )  # Sum counts across matching subsets for multiple populations faust_count_get_pop(   project_path = proj_path,   pop = list(     c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "+", "CD8-IgD" = "-"),     c("CD3" = "+", "CD4" = "-", "CD8-IgD" = "+")   ) )
